description: Name the build of this server: its version, the commit it was built from, and the digests of its capability document and its own image. Asking an installed CLI does not answer this -- a configured MCP process may be a different executable, which is how a pilot spent a pass on a defect the checkout had already fixed. Needs no plan and no repository.

description: List tasks whose blockers are all done, so an agent can pick real work.

name: aplan_verify

description: Create a task with an explicit id and phase, or mint the next id in this plan's own convention (including its configured ULID strategy) and derive the phase from its cut. It accepts live initial states, every creation-time relationship, revisit scheduling and version impact; terminal history uses the CLI's evidence-resolving manifest ledger. With `members`, both identity fields are required: create that milestone and move existing live work from its source cuts in one guarded batch. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after, by running the rules on the plan this would produce; what it would only warn about is named in `notes` instead.

cut.description: The cut to place it in: its milestone id (`M-v0.8`) or the label it reports itself under (`v0.8`). A plan with `require_cut_membership` rejects a task in no cut.

id.description: Explicit id. An ordinary add may omit it to mint from the plan convention; a non-empty members request requires it.

members.description: Existing live task ids moved from exactly one source cut each into the new milestone this add creates. A non-empty list requires id, phase and a tags entry equal to milestone, forbids cut, and reserves blocked_by for milestone predecessors.

paths.description: Globs this task owns. Without them its future evidence cannot be bound to it (`APLAN023`).

phase.description: Reporting phase. An ordinary add may omit it to derive from the selected cut or plan; a non-empty members request requires it.

revisit_at.description: RFC 3339 instant for an initially blocked task.

status.description: Initial live status. Terminal history uses the CLI evidence-resolving manifest ledger.

title.description: What the task is, in a line.

traces.description: Document sections this task answers to, as `path/to/doc.md#anchor`: what caused it, which exists, rather than what it will write. An anchor that does not resolve is refused (`APLAN008`).

version_impact_reason.description: Why the declared version impact applies.

name: aplan_add

description: One task whole: its `paths`, `traces` and `evidence`, which no other tool returns, plus what the graph resolves (its cut, whether it is ready, what it waits on and what it releases) and every finding attached to it. Reads repository-backed evidence and retained typed provider observations without starting configured processes; `aplan_verify` explicitly refreshes providers.

name: aplan_show

description: Add or remove one dependency edge: `after` is the task that must finish first. `blocked_by` is the only ordering the model has and it was writable only at creation, so re-sequencing meant editing files by hand. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after: a cycle, an id that does not exist, a cancelled blocker, or a done task acquiring an unfinished one. A milestone's `blocked_by` is which tasks are in that cut rather than what it comes after, so editing that is refused here and belongs to `aplan mv`.

add.description: True to record the edge, false to remove it.

after.description: The task it comes after, which must finish first.

name: aplan_dep

description: Close a task with evidence, resolved at L2 before it is written: a cited commit must be reachable from HEAD and touch the task's `paths`, a cited file must exist, and a cited test must be one a configured runner lists. Refuses exactly what the CLI refuses; evidence is a citation to be resolved, never a score the caller asserts. This agent tool never runs a test; it never starts `test.run` or `test.batch`. Focused L3 closure is an explicit trusted CLI or interactive action. It never fetches a url, and whatever nothing here could check is named in `unchecked` rather than left looking like a pass. `aplan_verify` resolves the whole plan.

evidence.description: Evidence as `kind:ref`, e.g. `commit:d213c9a`, `test:mod::name`, `file:path`, `url:https://...`. Required: a status is a claim, and this server will not make it without proof to resolve.

name: aplan_close

description: Record that you are working on a task, so other agents sharing this Git repository and all of its linked worktrees can see the same local ephemeral claim. It never edits the task or its durable `owner`. Two agents cannot both be told they hold one task: the common-directory record is a compare-and-swap. Taking a held task needs `from` naming the displaced holder. Labels are attribution, not authentication; the response includes time, origin, source and coordination scope.

as.description: The name to record. Otherwise `APLAN_OWNER`, then per-user `me`, this repository's `git config user.name`, then the operating system's user. Never read from `.aplan.yml`.

from.description: Who the task is being taken from. Required when somebody holds it, and checked rather than taken on trust.

A missing task's orphaned local claim can still be released explicitly. Releasing a visible task nobody holds changes nothing and says so.

description: Record that work on a task has begun, setting `in_progress`. A claim rather than a proof, and checked like one: `aplan_verify` reports `APLAN053` where the repository holds nothing matching the task's `paths`, so a status nobody acted on does not pass as progress. Refuses a task that is already terminal, because nothing reopens finished work.
